parts.visual:
The company missed its revenue targets. The runway is at 4 months. The CEO has to fire 50 people tomorrow, or the company will completely die. The CEO is physically sick to their stomach.

The Execution:
1. The Cut: Layoffs (RIF - Reduction in Force) are the ultimate test of a CEO's humanity and leadership.
2. The Rule: Cut once, and cut deep. If you only cut 10% of the team, the survivors will spend the next year terrified that they are next. If you cut 30% all at once, you secure the runway and the survivors can focus on rebuilding.
parts.audio: Firing one bad employee is hard. Firing 50 good people because you, the CEO, made a strategic mistake, is a nightmare. How you handle a mass layoff will dictate whether the remaining employees stay or immediately quit.

questions.question: A CEO realizes they need to lay off 40 people to survive. They decide to lay off 10 people this month, wait to see if things improve, and maybe lay off another 10 people next month. Why is this a catastrophic mistake?
options: Death by a Thousand Cuts. It completely destroys psychological safety. The remaining employees will stop working entirely, paralyzed by the fear that there will be another round of firings next week. They will all start looking for new jobs.
questions.correct_answer: Death by a Thousand Cuts. It completely destroys psychological safety. The remaining employees will stop working entirely, paralyzed by the fear that there will be another round of firings next week. They will all start looking for new jobs.
questions.explanation: Do the surgery once, not in small pieces.

questions.question: Listen to the CEO's speech to the company after a massive layoff. What is the key element of the speech?
questions.tts_text: We let go of 30 incredible people today. This is not their fault. It is my fault. I over-hired, I misread the market, and I failed you. I take 100% of the responsibility for this failure.
options: Extreme Ownership. A great CEO takes absolute personal responsibility for the layoffs. Blaming the economy, the VCs, or the employees themselves is cowardly and will destroy the trust of the surviving team.
questions.correct_answer: Extreme Ownership. A great CEO takes absolute personal responsibility for the layoffs. Blaming the economy, the VCs, or the employees themselves is cowardly and will destroy the trust of the surviving team.

questions.question: What is 'Severance' and why is it critical during a layoff?
options: A financial package (e.g., 3 months of salary) given to the fired employees. It is the ethical thing to do, it protects the company from lawsuits, and it shows the surviving employees that the company is humane.
questions.correct_answer: A financial package (e.g., 3 months of salary) given to the fired employees. It is the ethical thing to do, it protects the company from lawsuits, and it shows the surviving employees that the company is humane.
questions.explanation: How you treat the people leaving dictates how the people staying will perform.

questions.question: What is the worst possible way to lay off an employee?
options: Via a mass email or a pre-recorded Zoom webinar where they cannot speak or ask questions. It is deeply dehumanizing and often results in massive public backlash on social media.
questions.correct_answer: Via a mass email or a pre-recorded Zoom webinar where they cannot speak or ask questions. It is deeply dehumanizing and often results in massive public backlash on social media.
questions.explanation: You must look them in the eye, even through a screen.

questions.question: Order the words to describe the brutal rule of layoffs:
questions.explanation: The only way to survive the darkest day.
